newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu leaves Zaire ship, status of talks unclear.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu leaves Zaire ship, status of talks unclear.

text.p: Ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko left a South African ship late on Friday after rebel leader Laurent Kabila failed to appear for talks at sea to end Zaire's civil war, witnesses said.

Mobutu, who had sailed with South Africa's Nelson Mandela into international waters off West Africa for a planned rendezvous with Kabila, left the SAS Outeniqua at Congo's port of Pointe Noire -- where he and Mandela boarded earlier in the day.

The status of the talks was not immediately clear but Kabila said in Angola's capital Luanda earlier on Friday he had not written them off and could travel to the ship on Saturday if he received satisfactory security guarantees.
"I will go to the ship tomorrow if I receive adequate assurances from the South Africans tomorrow that security arrangements are in place," Kabila told a news conference.
"If we wanted to we could win this militarily in two weeks," he said. "Suggestions that I am stalling for time are ridiculous. I am interested in finding a peaceful solution to the problem."
Mobutu has a house in Pointe Noire. There was no sign of Mandela leaving the ship, a converted Russian-built icebreaker.
